name: Daniel Martinez
chief_complaint: Abdominal pain that started around my belly button and moved to the right lower abdomen
opening_statement: The pain started yesterday around my belly button, just a dull ache. But overnight it moved to my right lower belly and got much sharper. I feel nauseous and I vomited once this morning. I can't eat anything.
emotional_baseline: Uncomfortable, guarding abdomen, cooperative with examination

symptoms.symptom: Right iliac fossa pain (classic appendicitis migration)

socrates.onset: Periumbilical pain 24h ago → migrated to RIF 12h ago
socrates.character: Initially dull periumbilical → now sharp, constant RIF pain

rag_citation.source: eTG Surgery 8.3.1: Acute Appendicitis - Clinical Features
rag_citation.quote: Classic appendicitis: periumbilical pain migrating to right iliac fossa over 12-24h with anorexia and vomiting

symptoms.symptom: Anorexia (loss of appetite - UNIVERSAL in appendicitis)

rag_citation.quote: Anorexia is present in >95% of appendicitis cases - absence argues against diagnosis
Nausea/vomiting occur AFTER pain onset in appendicitis (vs gastroenteritis where vomiting precedes pain)
Low-grade fever (<38.5°C) typical of uncomplicated appendicitis - high fever suggests perforation

examination_findings.general: Appears uncomfortable, lying still, flushed, guarding abdomen

abdomen.inspection: Moving with respiration but reduced movement, no distension, no visible masses
abdomen.palpation: Maximal tenderness at McBurney's point (RIF), localized guarding (involuntary), rebound tenderness POSITIVE (peritonism), Rovsing's sign POSITIVE (RIF pain on LIF palpation), psoas sign POSITIVE (pain on right hip extension - retrocecal appendix)
abdomen.rectal_exam: Tender on right side (supports RIF pathology)

examination_findings.cardiovascular: Normal heart sounds, capillary refill <2 seconds

investigations.urinalysis: No blood, no protein, no nitrites (excludes UTI/renal colic)
investigations.bhcg: Negative (female of childbearing age - must exclude ectopic pregnancy)
investigations.ct_abdomen_pelvis:
ONLY if diagnosis uncertain (Alvarado score 5-6) - this case clinically obvious:
    - Inflamed appendix 12mm diameter (normal <6mm)
    - Periappendiceal fat stranding
    - No abscess, no perforation
investigations.ultrasound: Alternative to CT (especially in children/young women) - non-compressible appendix >6mm

expected_management: IMMEDIATE MANAGEMENT:
1. Keep patient nil by mouth (NBM) - prepare for surgery
2. IV access (14G or 16G) + IV fluids 0.9% NaCl 1L over 4h (dehydration from vomiting)
3. Analgesia: Morphine 5-10mg IV PRN (pain relief does NOT mask diagnosis - outdated myth)
4. Antiemetics: Metoclopramide 10mg IV or ondansetron 4mg IV
ANTIBIOTICS (PREOPERATIVE):
5. Single-dose prophylactic antibiotics BEFORE incision:
- Cefazolin 2g IV + metronidazole 500mg IV (within 60 min of incision)
- If penicillin allergy: Gentamicin 5mg/kg IV + metronidazole 500mg IV
- Prophylaxis reduces wound infection by 50%
SURGICAL MANAGEMENT (DEFINITIVE TREATMENT):
6. Laparoscopic appendicectomy (PREFERRED):
- Advantages: shorter hospital stay, faster recovery, less pain, better cosmesis
- Approach: 3 ports (umbilical camera, RIF working ports)
- Remove appendix, irrigate peritoneal cavity
7. Open appendicectomy (McBurney incision):
- If laparoscopy unavailable or perforated appendix with abscess
IF PERFORATED APPENDICITIS (NOT this case):
8. Signs of perforation:
- High fever >38.5°C, severe tachycardia, diffuse peritonitis
- Prolonged symptoms >72h
- Palpable RIF mass (appendix abscess)
9. Management of perforation:
- Prolonged antibiotics (5-7 days IV then oral)
- Consider interval appendicectomy if abscess (drain abscess → antibiotics 6-8 weeks → elective appendicectomy)
POSTOPERATIVE MANAGEMENT:
10. Early mobilization (within 4-6h post-op)
11. Resume oral intake when tolerated (clear fluids → normal diet)
12. Discharge home same day or next day (uncomplicated laparoscopic appendicectomy)
13. Wound care: waterproof dressings, remove in 7-10 days (or absorbable sutures)
14. Return to normal activities in 1-2 weeks (laparoscopic) or 4-6 weeks (open)
DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS (EXCLUDED):
15. Mesenteric adenitis (viral URTI, younger children, less focal tenderness)
16. Gastroenteritis (vomiting BEFORE pain, diarrhea prominent)
17. Ectopic pregnancy (females - excluded by βhCG)
18. Renal colic (radiation to groin, hematuria on urinalysis)
19. Ovarian torsion (females, sudden severe pain, adnexal mass on imaging)

critical_errors.error: Delayed surgery in clinically obvious appendicitis (waiting for CT unnecessarily)
critical_errors.explanation: Alvarado score ≥7 indicates high probability - clinical diagnosis sufficient, CT delays treatment and increases perforation risk

critical_errors.error: Withheld analgesia (morphine) due to myth that pain relief masks diagnosis
critical_errors.explanation: Analgesia does NOT mask appendicitis signs - withholding causes unnecessary suffering (outdated practice)

critical_errors.error: Failed to give preoperative prophylactic antibiotics (cefazolin + metronidazole)
critical_errors.explanation: Prophylactic antibiotics reduce wound infection by 50% - must be given within 60 min of incision

critical_errors.error: Missed perforated appendicitis (high fever, prolonged symptoms >72h, palpable mass)
critical_errors.explanation: Perforated appendicitis requires prolonged antibiotics +/- interval appendicectomy - immediate appendicectomy in abscess cavity increases complications

critical_errors.error: Failed to exclude ectopic pregnancy in female of childbearing age (did not order βhCG)
critical_errors.explanation: Ectopic pregnancy can mimic appendicitis - MUST exclude with βhCG before surgery in females

fracp_reviews.clinical_accuracy: Excellent - classic appendicitis presentation with migration pattern, Alvarado score calculation appropriate
fracp_reviews.difficulty_appropriate: Yes - Easy difficulty appropriate (classic presentation, straightforward diagnosis)
fracp_reviews.rag_citations_correct: Yes - eTG 8.3 citations verified and accurate
fracp_reviews.feedback: Excellent surgery persona. Classic appendicitis migration (periumbilical → RIF). Good emphasis on anorexia being universal (>95%). Consider adding Alvarado score explicit calculation for teaching (migration 1pt, anorexia 1pt, nausea 1pt, RIF tenderness 2pts, rebound 1pt, fever 1pt, leukocytosis 2pt = 8/10 high probability).

fracp_reviews.reviewer_credentials: FRACS, Emergency Surgery subspecialist, 14 years post-fellowship
fracp_reviews.clinical_accuracy: Accurate appendicitis management - appropriate use of clinical diagnosis without unnecessary CT
fracp_reviews.feedback: Good persona. Management pathway correct (clinical diagnosis → laparoscopic appendicectomy). Excellent debunking of analgesia myth (pain relief does NOT mask signs). Suggest mentioning Rovsing's sign and psoas sign explicitly as positive physical exam findings.

learning_objectives: Recognize classic appendicitis migration (periumbilical pain → RIF over 12-24h)
Understand Alvarado score (score ≥7 = high probability, proceed to surgery)
Perform RIF examination (McBurney's point, rebound tenderness, Rovsing's sign, psoas sign)
Understand anorexia is universal in appendicitis (>95% cases - absence argues against diagnosis)
Debunk myth: analgesia does NOT mask appendicitis diagnosis (provide pain relief)
Give preoperative prophylactic antibiotics (cefazolin + metronidazole within 60 min of incision)
Differentiate uncomplicated vs perforated appendicitis (fever, duration, palpable mass)
Exclude ectopic pregnancy in females (βhCG mandatory before surgery)
